_comment: Pinned FFmpeg builds, one per Tauri target triple.
Pinning is not bureaucracy here: three lab machines must encode identically,
and two different FFmpeg builds can differ in default x264 tuning, in which
input pixel formats they negotiate, and in how -fps_mode cfr rounds. The
version string below is written into every recording manifest, so 'were these
two sessions produced the same way?' is answerable after the fact.
sha256 starts as null. Run `npm run ffmpeg -- --pin` once per target to
download, print, and write the real checksum back into this file. After that
every fetch verifies against it and a silently-rotated upstream build fails
loudly instead of drifting into the data.
macOS entries have not been exercised on real hardware yet — the lab Mac is
flagged as unverified across the repo's notes. Expect to adjust these URLs on

x86_64-pc-windows-msvc._note: gyan.dev keeps no stable per-version URL, so this points at the rolling release build. That is exactly why the checksum pin matters: when gyan rotates the build the fetch fails loudly and someone re-pins on purpose, rather than a lab machine quietly acquiring a different encoder.
